headline: Walmart grew U.S. comps 4.1% on traffic but held its outlook as gas prices loom; shares dropped about 7%.
guidance_note: FY27 kept at 3.5-4.5% sales growth and adj. EPS $2.75-2.85 despite fuel headwind; Q2 guide seen as soft.
key_messages: Walmart U.S. comp ex fuel +4.1%, led by 3.0% transaction growth; average ticket +1.1%.
Sam's Club U.S. comp ex fuel +3.9% with transactions +6.2% but ticket -2.2%.
Global and Walmart U.S. eCommerce both +26%; eCommerce ~23% of net sales.
Higher fuel costs cost ~$175M (about 250 bps of operating income growth); CFO said impact likely larger in Q2.
General merchandise mix helped U.S. margin for first time in 18 quarters, partly thanks to larger tax refunds.

consumer.income_split: Higher-income shoppers spending with confidence; lower-income consumers more budget conscious and showing financial stress.
consumer.big_ticket: General merchandise improved, but management said bigger tax refunds likely gave it a temporary lift.
consumer.pricing: Absorbing higher fuel costs rather than passing them on while keeping guidance.
consumer.quote: "We're absorbing those prices and still maintaining our guidance, and I feel really good about that." - CFO John David Rainey on fuel costs

macro_read: Spending held up in spring 2026 helped by tax refunds, but a widening income split and rising gas prices signaled pressure building for lower-income households.
